messages:
maria: FYI secret-scanner found a GitHub App private key blob in partner logs (partner-logs/2026-03-20/ingest-blob.pem) — looks like raw PEM landed in a gz archive :rotating_light:

secret-scanner: matched pattern '-----BEGIN (RSA )?PRIVATE KEY-----' in gs://partner-logs/2026/03/20/ingest-blob.pem (blob id z9y8x7). confidence 0.98.

maria: tagging eng-security for triage. suspect the partner's deploy process uploaded artifacts without redaction.

dmitri: can we confirm it's the actual GitHub App key vs some unrelated key? any nearby context lines?

maria: snippet (redacted):
```
-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\nMIIEvQIBADANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAASC...\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----\n```
and a few lines later: "installation_id=12345 app_id=9876"

akash: that ties it to the app. immediate actions we should take:
- block/uninstall the installation to prevent token issuance
- rotate GH app private key + revoke any installation tokens
- snapshot evidence and replace exposed blobs with redacted placeholder
- assess if any Vault auth roles reference the app and rotate those creds
- if wrapped ciphertexts found, plan KMS/rewrap or key rotation

sara: i'll run a targeted search across partner log buckets and any recent backups. running: gsutil cat gs://partner-logs/2026/03/** | rg "BEGIN PRIVATE KEY" -n --hidden
found blobs: z9y8x7, y6x5w4, p0o9i8 (3 matches). copying originals to gs://sec-evidence/4876549999/ then overwriting with redacted stub file.

dmitri: i'll start GH App key rotation. steps: generate new keypair, update app settings, then rotate tokens. sample commands i'll run locally:
```
openssl genrsa -out ghapp_new.pem 4096
# verify and upload via GitHub API/console
```
I'll also check installation activity logs for token creation/forged calls.

maria: @legal-bot please advise on partner notification and data handling. we need to know disclosure obligations.

legal-bot: please provide: affected partner name, list of affected blobs, timeline of discovery, any evidence of token misuse. legal recommends low-band disclosure and hold on external statements until we confirm scope.

akash: Vault/KMS considerations: if partner uploaded a wrapped ciphertext (we saw ci-kms-ciphertext markers nearby in one blob), we need to determine whether the ciphertext was uploaded alongside the PEM (i.e., both present). if so, the wrapped ciphertext may include ciphertext of other secrets but not directly compromised. plan:
- lock down transit/unwrap permissions to rotation SA only
- create new KMS key version or new key and re-encrypt important blobs if necessary
- rewrap affected ciphertexts after ensuring app key is rotated to prevent abuse of tokens to call unwrap during rotation window

dmitri: agree. prioritize app key rotation first, then any rewraps. also update CI that signs webhooks with the app key.

sara: scrub job completed for the three blobs. originals copied to evidence bucket (read-only) and redacted placeholders uploaded with message: "REDACTED: private key removed by security; contact security@redwood.com for incident reference 4876549999." set lifecycle to 90 days in the evidence bucket for forensic review.

maria: assigning owners: uninstall/block app = @maria, rotate GH app key + update integrations = @dmitri, scrub & notify partner = @sara, Vault/KMS follow-up = @akash, legal comms = @legal-bot.

akash: pushing a temporary RBAC change on Vault: narrow transit/rewrap to 'rotation-sa' and revoke broad group 'devops' unwrap perms. will open vault-policy PR and set a 24h auto-rollback annotation.

dmitri: timeline proposal: 0-30m: disable installation + block webhooks; 30-90m: generate+upload new app key + revoke tokens; 90-240m: scrub logs + evidence capture + notify partner; 4-24h: rewrap/rotate KMS keys if any ciphertexts impacted; 24-72h: follow-up audit and postmortem.

maria: question: should we rotate any customer-facing keys or just app keys and related installation tokens?

akash: only rotate customer-facing keys if we find evidence they were derived from the exposed key or used by the malicious actor. otherwise rotate app key + any role tokens that directly trusted the app.

sara: partner SRE responded and confirmed they will delete local copies and audit their deploy pipeline. they've asked for our scrub log and evidence manifest. i've shared a redacted manifest and evidence bucket read-only link.

dmitri: will scan GH audit logs for suspicious JWT usage and revocations. also add a detection rule to secret-scanner for PEM patterns inside compressed archives to reduce false negatives.

maria: logging: flag all API calls from app_id=9876 in the last 48h and export to sec-evidence. setting an alert for any token minting from that installation.

akash: after rotation we'll schedule a short maintenance window to re-encrypt any dependent blobs with a new KMS key version and rotate Vault tokens issued to the app's service accounts.

legal-bot: legal will draft the partner notification template. hold for 1h while we confirm no active misuse.

sara: scrub completion timestamp: 2026-03-20T12:55:20Z. evidence copied to gs://sec-evidence/4876549999/. shared link with partner SRE.

dmitri: creating follow-up checklist and postmortem doc in #postmortems. will tag owners and follow-ups.

maria: thanks everyone. i'll update here as each milestone completes. :white_check_mark:
